title: Why get an expensive Pi when I have an old phone?
why_read: A practical, hands-on hacker idea about repurposing old smartphones as cheap embedded computers instead of buying a Raspberry Pi.
analysis: The piece argues that old smartphones often outperform a Raspberry Pi in CPU, GPU, storage, and battery while being free or very cheap to acquire. It likely covers practical considerations like running Linux or Android-based setups, dealing with proprietary bootloaders, and power management differences from the Pi ecosystem. For engineers interested in hobby electronics, this is a useful, grounded discussion about tradeoffs in repurposing hardware rather than buying new boards. It's a familiar topic in maker circles but still carries genuine practical value.
